question: Is there a cap on how many vacation days I can take in a year?
reference_answer: No. There is no set annual limit on PTO. Time off longer than 25 consecutive calendar days needs special permission from your manager, your People Business Partner and the Absence Management team.

question: How far ahead do I need to tell my manager if I want to take 3 days off?
reference_answer: Give at least twice as many days of notice as the time off you plan to take, so 6 business days of notice for 3 days off.

question: How many paid sick days do I get, and when do they start?
reference_answer: Up to 25 paid sick days, available from your first day of work, counted over a rolling 12-month period.

question: I'm ill today. Can I just log it as PTO instead of sick time?
reference_answer: No. PTO may not be substituted for sick time. Time off for medical needs, physical or mental, goes under the Sick Time policy.

question: What is the minimum amount of time off the company recommends I take each year?
reference_answer: At least two consecutive weeks off, and a minimum of 25 days in total across the year.

question: How long is paid parental leave, and by when does it have to be used?
reference_answer: 16 weeks of paid parental leave. It must be used before the child's first birthday, or the first anniversary of the adoption or foster placement.

question: Can I use caregiver sick time to make my parental leave longer?
reference_answer: No, not unless you have a family member with a serious health condition. For extra time you can use flexible PTO, coordinated with your manager.

question: What is the most I can spend on a hotel per night on a work trip?
reference_answer: Up to $300 USD per night including tax for a standard room, booked with 7 days of lead time.

question: What is the daily meal allowance when I travel for work?
reference_answer: Meals while travelling on company business are reimbursable up to $120 USD per day.

question: I bought something for work four months ago and forgot to claim it. Can I still get reimbursed?
reference_answer: Not automatically. Expense claims more than 90 days after the purchase date are not reimbursed unless your manager approves.

question: Can I put a $6,000 purchase through Navan as an expense?
reference_answer: No. A single item up to $5,000 can be expensed in Navan. Anything above $5,000 has to go through the procurement process in Zip.

question: How much will the company pay towards a co-working space?
reference_answer: Up to $700 per month, with pre-approval. Only the rent is covered, not deposits, travel, parking or meals.

question: What is the limit for home internet reimbursement, and is the router covered?
reference_answer: The monthly internet service charge is reimbursable up to $100. Hardware such as routers and extenders, setup fees and insurance are not covered.

question: Is there a yearly budget for upgrading my home office setup?
reference_answer: Yes. Existing team members get a yearly refresh of 500 USD for home office upgrades, provided they were employed for the entire previous calendar year.

question: Is there a ceiling on the total expenses I can claim in one month?
reference_answer: Yes, $10K USD per month. Beyond that every item needs approval from the Accounts Payable team. For E-Group members the limit is $20K.

question: If I pay for a $100 monitor partly with a $50 gift card, how much do I get back?
reference_answer: $50. Only the actual out-of-pocket amount charged to your own payment method is reimbursed.

question: How much can I claim per year for courses and training?
reference_answer: Up to $10,000 per calendar year from the Growth and Development Fund, for eligible and approved learning.

question: If the company pays for my university course and I resign, do I have to pay it back?
reference_answer: Yes, if you leave voluntarily before completing twelve consecutive months of active employment: academic study or tuition expenses of $1,000 USD or more must be refunded.

question: I'm going to a conference. Which budget pays for the ticket, which pays for the hotel, and what is the nightly hotel limit?
reference_answer: The registration fee comes from the Growth and Development Fund. Travel, lodging and meals are expensed separately under the travel and expense policy, from your department's travel budget. Hotels are reimbursable up to $300 USD per night.

question: What is the minimum vacation entitlement for employees in Germany?
reference_answer: At least 20 vacation days, accruing from the start date at 1.67 days per month.

question: For a sales role with $100,000 on-target earnings and a 60/40 split, what is the base salary?
reference_answer: $60,000 base salary and a $40,000 commission target. On-target earnings is base salary plus the commission target.

question: Am I allowed to watch a film on my company laptop?
reference_answer: Yes. Private use of company property, such as checking personal email or watching a movie, is allowed as long as it does not break the law, harm the company or interfere with intellectual property.

question: How do I declare a production incident?
reference_answer: Type /incident or /inc in Slack and follow the prompts to open an incident.

question: For which incident severities is the engineer on call paged automatically?
reference_answer: Only for S1 and S2 incidents.
must_include: only paged automatically for S1 or S2

question: An S3 incident came in on Saturday. Does it have to be mitigated over the weekend?
reference_answer: No. The engineer on call still responds to the alert, but mitigation for severity 3 and 4 incidents can wait for normal business hours, Monday to Friday. Only severity 1 and 2 are mitigated at the weekend.

question: What exactly counts as a degraded service?
reference_answer: Any sustained 5-minute period in which a service is below its documented Apdex SLO or above its documented error ratio SLO.

question: I'm reporting an incident and I'm not sure how bad it is, but many customers seem affected. Which severity do I choose?
reference_answer: Choose S1 or S2. When unsure it is better to err towards the higher severity; it can be adjusted later.

question: How quickly must an Incident Manager On Call respond to an escalation?
reference_answer: Within 15 minutes. There is a 15 minute SLA to respond to escalations.

question: Who is eligible to join the Incident Manager rotation?
reference_answer: Team members in the Engineering group at job grades 8 and 9, in any job family except Customer Support, who have been employed for at least 3 months and are not already on another time-critical on-call rotation.

question: How long should a newly launched service have Tier 2 on-call coverage?
reference_answer: A new feature or service arriving through the Component Owner Model should have a 24x5 Tier 2 subject matter expert for at least the first six months.

question: What are the data classification levels?
reference_answer: Four levels: Red, Orange, Yellow and Green. Red is the most sensitive and Green is publicly shareable.

question: How is personal data classified, and is anything exempt?
reference_answer: Personal data is Orange. The exception is team member names, work email addresses and GitLab usernames, which are Yellow.

question: Who do I ask if I can't work out how a piece of data should be classified?
reference_answer: The Security Risk team, in Slack via @security-risk.

question: Can I copy Red data from its approved system into another tool?
reference_answer: Not without approval. Red data may not be transmitted from an approved Red data source to any other system without first getting approval from the Privacy and Security teams.

question: Who does the on-call security engineer page to escalate a security incident?
reference_answer: The Security Incident Manager On Call (SIMOC), who directs the response and coordinates communication.

question: What inherent risk level does a vendor get if it handles Red data?
reference_answer: Critical.

question: How many vendor bids do I need for a new $150K purchase?
reference_answer: Two to three. Spend between $100K and $250K needs a business-led RFP with 2-3 vendor bids.

question: How long does the legal review step of a purchase request take?
reference_answer: 3 to 21 days.

question: Can I buy a software subscription on my own card and expense it?
reference_answer: No. Software charged to a personal or corporate credit card is denied for reimbursement. Individual use software goes through the Procurement request process and is paid with a virtual card after approval, up to $5,000 per person per year.

question: When is a purchase order required?
reference_answer: For any purchase or service with a total contract value over $5000, unless it falls under the PO Exception Policy.

question: Can Accounts Payable pay a supplier by cheque?
reference_answer: No. Suppliers are paid by NetSuite electronic payment, ACH or wire only. Accounts Payable does not issue check payments.

question: An invoice came in above the purchase order amount. How much overage is tolerated?
reference_answer: Invoices have a 10% PO tolerance. Overages beyond it up to $1,000 USD are reviewed by Accounts Payable and routed to FP&A for approval; above $1,000 they are not processed and need a PO change request.

question: What quote types can I create for a deal?
reference_answer: Four: New Subscription, Amend Existing, Renew Existing and Cancel Existing.

question: How far in the future can a quote start date be for an order to be processed?
reference_answer: The quote start date must be within 30 calendar days of the date the order is submitted.

question: Which team does Sales Commissions sit in?
reference_answer: Sales Commissions is part of Field Operations and reports into Sales Operations.
